title: The Oath of Ironhollow
premise: Oscar Eriksen has survived three years in Ironhollow by keeping his beast-speaker gift small and secret, charming rats and pigeons for coin in a city where magic is a hanging offense. When his new love, Wren Calloway, appears verbatim in a century-old book of prophecies, Oscar learns the prophecy names him too: the one who will unbind King Aldric from the crown-spirit that has worn him as a puppet for a decade. As the crown's hunters close in on both of them, Oscar must choose between the safe anonymity he built and the dangerous belonging Wren offers. In the end, Oscar speaks to the ancient iron of the throne itself, convincing it to release its grip; Aldric dies free, the prophecy breaks unfulfilled, and Oscar chooses exile with Wren over a pardon that would require his silence.
about_author: Sable Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people caught in loud destinies, and live somewhere north of anywhere important.

chapters.title: The Rat Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Oscar charms rats for gossip and pigeons for messages, scraping by under Ironhollow's magic laws, until a chance meeting at a night market introduces him to Wren Calloway. A rat warns him she smells of old iron and danger. Emotional beat: longing — Oscar wants connection but has taught himself that wanting things gets people hanged.

chapters.title: A Century of Waiting Ink
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, then Wren. Wren reveals her family guards a prophetic codex; Oscar finds himself and their date written on its pages, dated tomorrow. The crown's witch-hunters raid Wren's home, forcing them to flee into the undercity together. Emotional beat: vertigo — intimacy accelerates unnaturally because fate has already scripted them, and both resent being read like text.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Guided by the codex and beasts of the deep tunnels, they reach the sealed throne room and learn the truth: King Aldric bargained with the iron crown to save his dying city, and it consumed him. Hunters corner them; Wren takes a wound meant for Oscar. Emotional beat: fury and grief — Oscar realizes the prophecy ends with Wren's death unless he breaks it first.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. At dawn, Oscar does what no mage attempted: he stops commanding and starts listening, speaking to the crown's iron as a lonely, bound thing. It releases Aldric, who dies human and grateful; the prophecy shatters, sparing Wren. Offered a pardon if he swears silence forever, Oscar refuses and leaves with Wren. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely, not fated.
